claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy with a dendritic microstructure.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a lower-temperature yield strength of approximately 800 MPa.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding approximately 0.5–1 at% Y to TiVNbTa will produce nanoscale Y2O3 particles during processing.
The resulting Y2O3 particles will stabilize the dendritic BCC structure at 1273 K.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will pin grain boundaries in the modified TiVNbTa alloy.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will impede dislocation climb and other thermally activated dislocation motion.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will inhibit grain coarsening at elevated temperature.
Grain coarsening and thermally activated deformation contribute to elevated-temperature softening.
Precipitation strengthening and grain refinement can increase the mechanical strength of a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Y addition will increase the yield and compressive strengths of TiVNbTa at 1273 K relative to the 330 MPa yield-strength baseline.
The Y-modified alloy will retain adequate ductility for use as a thermal-transfer layer.
The proposed operating and testing boundary is approximately 1273 K and 30–40% mechanical strain under thermal cycling representative of a W/CuCrZr intermediate layer.
The magnitude of strengthening will depend on Y2O3 dispersion and processing-dependent grain size and oxide morphology.
A controlled comparison of Y-free and 0.5–1 at% Y-containing samples processed identically can test the proposed strengthening effect.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant strength improvement, or failure to observe a well-dispersed Y2O3 population, would falsify the hypothesis.
